# Repo Orientation (auto-generated by repo-orient, do not hand-edit)

- Generated from commit: `ded2ae53fb0387604559e35b0279ccbeead0499a`
- Generated: 2026-08-14

## Overview

`patch_refiner` is a small, single-crate Rust library + optional CLI (~880 lines
across `src/`) that validates AI-generated patch candidates **syntactically** —
does a unified diff parse, and does it apply cleanly to the original source —
for use in automated-program-repair (APR) pipelines, primarily as a dependency
of a sibling project called `ruchat`. It deliberately does not run compile,
test, or lint commands; that's delegated to the calling system. This boundary
is enforced as an explicit architectural invariant (`.claude/rules/scope-
boundary.md`), not just a README claim: `SemanticChecksConfig` fields are
parsed and validated but never wired to `std::process::Command` anywhere in
the crate, and `DiagnosticCategory::Compile`/`::Test` exist in the schema but
are never constructed.

The crate has four "modes," resolved by `resolve_mode` from `mode_override`
(if set) or from the number/shape of supplied `perfect_patches`: Mode 3 is
pure parse+apply (no comparison); Modes 1/2/4 additionally compare the
candidate's applied result against one or more "perfect" reference patches,
scoring the closeness of a non-matching candidate via a hand-rolled,
regression-prone lexer (`compute_distance`/`ChangeSet` in `core.rs`) that
classifies diff tokens into code/string/comment regions to weight the
distance score. That lexer is explicitly flagged in
`.claude/rules/compute-distance-lexer.md` as having caused multiple subtle
regressions and needing careful, test-covered changes only.

**The single most consequential fact about the current state of this repo:
`master` has zero tests.** A 19-test suite covering exactly the lexer's
documented ambiguous-input failure modes (raw strings, `//`/`/* */` markers
arriving as separate tokens, empty string literals, `resolve_mode`
precedence) exists, but only on two orphaned local branches (`with_tests` at
`e4e62da`, `shex_with_tests` at `69edd2b`) that were never merged forward —
master has since moved 7–11 commits past their merge-bases. Both
`.claude/rules/compute-distance-lexer.md` and `ROADMAP_BACKLOG.md`'s
"confirmed resolved" table describe this test suite as if it exists on the
working branch; it does not. This is a real, fixable gap (cherry-pick or
merge the test module back in), not a documentation-only nit.

Two smaller, confirmed doc/reality gaps: README.md's Quickstart never
mentions `--features cli`, so following it literally builds only the library,
not the `patch-refiner` binary. And ROADMAP.md's three "Now" (next-up) items —
richer apply-failure diagnostics with real file content, pre-parse repair of
malformed diffs, and documenting the "never trust model-written `@@` offsets"
invariant as a code comment — are all still unstarted in source, consistent
with the roadmap's own framing of them as planned work, not claimed-done work.

## Investigation topics

### `src/core.rs` — the evaluation engine

`PatchRefiner::evaluate(req) -> Result<RefinementResponse>` (core.rs:282) is
the sole public entry point. It validates `schema_version` against
`models::SCHEMA_VERSION`, validates config, calls `resolve_mode` (core.rs:313
— `mode_override` wins if set; else `perfect_patches.len()`/`.reason` maps to
Mode1 (1 patch + reason) / Mode2 (1 patch, no reason) / Mode3 (0 patches) /
Mode4 (2+ patches)), then dispatches to `evaluate_mode_3` (core.rs:501, pure
`diffy::Patch::from_str` + `diffy::apply`, first candidate that applies wins,
`Approved`/`Failed`) or `evaluate_modes_1_2_4` (core.rs:387, applies each
candidate and each perfect patch, exact-match → `Approved`, else scores the
best `Deviation` via `compute_distance` and returns `Rejected`).

`compute_distance`/`ChangeSet` (core.rs:117–385) is the hand-rolled lexer:
single-pass, classifies diff tokens into code/string/raw-string/comment
regions using buffered multi-char markers (`//`, `/* */`, `#"…"#`), tracks
ambiguous "hypotheses" as a `Vec<Run>` deduped on a normalized/reversed
record (not the raw token, per the rule), scored by `hypothesis_score`. It's
purely a ranking signal for Mode1/2/4 deviations — Mode3 never touches it and
it plays no role in any pass/fail decision.

No pre-parse repair step exists before either `Patch::from_str` call site
(core.rs:399, 426, 517) — malformed diffs (e.g. missing leading space on
context lines) are not auto-repaired today; this is open work, matching
ROADMAP.md's "Now" list, not a claimed-done feature.

**Test coverage — confirmed gap.** `grep -rn "#\[cfg(test)\]\|#\[test\]" src/`
on master returns nothing. The rule files and `ROADMAP_BACKLOG.md` describe
tests (including `test_resolve_mode` and several ambiguous-marker regression
tests) that exist only on unmerged branches `with_tests` (`e4e62da`) and
`shex_with_tests` (`69edd2b`) — see "Overview" above.

### `src/models.rs` — request/response schema

`RefinementRequest`: `schema_version`, `original_code`, `candidates`,
`perfect_patches`, `problem_statement` (accepted, never read by `evaluate`),
`config` (→ `RefinementConfig`: `mode_override`, `language`, `file_path`,
`semantic_checks: SemanticChecksConfig`, `language_weights`,
`whitespace: WhitespaceConfig`). `RefinementResponse`: `schema_version`,
`mode`, `decision` (Approved/Rejected/Failed), `selected_patch_id`,
`matched_perfect_patch_id`, `deviations`, `reasoning`, `diagnostics`.

`SCHEMA_VERSION` (models.rs:4, `"1.0"`) is a single const; all four
`RefinementResponse` construction sites in core.rs read it via
`crate::models::SCHEMA_VERSION.to_string()` rather than a hardcoded literal —
structurally impossible for request-check and response-value to drift apart,
satisfying the invariant in `.claude/rules/patch-application.md`.

`SemanticChecksConfig` (`run_compile_check`, `run_tests`, `compile_command`,
`test_command`, `timeout_secs`) is validated for shape (e.g.
`run_compile_check` requires `compile_command`) but never read to spawn a
process anywhere in the crate — confirmed via an empty
`grep -rn "Command::new\|std::process" src/`. `DiagnosticCategory` has 6
variants (`PatchParse`, `PatchApply`, `Compile`, `Test`, `Similarity`,
`Other`); only the first two and `Other` are ever constructed — `Compile` and
`Test` are reserved-only, matching `.claude/rules/scope-boundary.md`.

### `src/bin/patch-refiner.rs` — CLI binary

Reads `--input <path>` or, if omitted, all of stdin; writes exactly one
pretty-printed JSON `RefinementResponse` to stdout via a single `println!`
(no other prints anywhere in `src/`, confirmed by grep — this matches the
intent behind commit `30f6b34`, "Debug stdout/stderr corrupting CLI JSON
contract - delete."). CLI args: `--input`/`-i`, `--mode`,
`--ignore-whitespace`, `--language`.

The binary and its `clap` dependency are feature-gated: `clap` is
`optional = true`, `[features] cli = ["clap"]`, and the `[[bin]]` has
`required-features = ["cli"]` — a plain `cargo build` builds only the
library. **README.md's Quickstart never mentions `--features cli`** (grep
confirms zero occurrences of "cli"/"feature" in README.md), so following it
literally will not build or run the binary.

`default_commands()` (patch-refiner.rs:25–32) is a pure `match language {...}`
returning command-string pairs (e.g. `"cargo build"`/`"cargo test"` for
Rust) — used only to fill in `compile_command`/`test_command` defaults in the
request config when unset, never to execute anything. Confirmed no
`Command::new`/`std::process` usage anywhere in `src/`.

### Roadmap vs. source — what's actually done

ROADMAP.md's "Now" theme lists three items, all confirmed **not started** in
source:
1. Apply-failure diagnostics including real file content (capped ~4000
   chars) — core.rs's apply-failure diagnostics are still a bare
   `format!("... apply failed: {}", e)`, no file content injected.
2. Pre-parse repair of common diff malformations — no such step exists

3. Documenting the "never reject based on model-written `@@` offsets"
   anti-pattern as an in-code comment — currently only exists in
   `.claude/rules/patch-application.md` and the roadmap docs; grep of

The "Next" theme (shadow-mode integration with `ruchat`) is explicitly gated
on "Now" closing first and has no started work: no path dependency in
Cargo.toml, no "shadow" references in `src/`.

`reviews/` (prior roadmap drafts, ruchat context docs, review-comment
threads) is a pure docs archive — not referenced by `src/` or `Cargo.toml`,
and is itself gitignored. `tags` (1.1MB, gitignored) is a ctags index.
`review.jsonl` (untracked, 24 lines) looks like output from a prior automated
anti-pattern review pass, referencing an absolute path outside this
container — not part of the crate. `Cargo.lock`/`.gitignore` are untracked
but standard.
